messages.content: When do I go on my next trip?

function.name: EventQuery
function.description: Search for calendar events that match a given text query within a user's calendar. The search considers both the title and description of the events. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

search_string.description: The text to search for within the title and description of an event.

start_date.description: The start date for the range of events to search, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the range of events to search, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_recurring.description: A flag to indicate whether to include recurring events in the search.

function.name: reschedule_event
function.description: Reschedule an event by assigning it a new date or time based on the provided ISO-8601 datetime string. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

event_identifier.description: A unique identifier for the event, such as a UUID.

new_datetime.description: The new date and time to which the event is being rescheduled, in ISO-8601 format (e.g., 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ').

message.reasoning: The user asks: "When do I go on my next trip?" We need to interpret that they want to know when their next trip is scheduled. We have a tool to search calendar events. We should search for events that might be trips. The user didn't specify a date range. We can search for events with "trip" or maybe "travel". But we don't know the user's calendar. We can ask clarifying question: "Do you have a calendar event for your next trip?" But we can also try to search for events with "trip" or "travel" in title/description. We can use the function EventQuery. Let's search for "trip" or "travel" within the next year. We can set start_date to today. But we don't know today's date. We can assume current date is 2026-05-31. So start_date: "2026-05-31", end_date: maybe "2027-05-31". Let's search for "trip" or "travel". But the function only accepts one search_string. We could combine: "trip OR travel". But not sure if the function supports OR. We can just search for "trip". That might catch many events. Or we can search for "travel". Let's search for "trip". We'll call EventQuery with search_string: "trip", start_date: "2026-05-31", end_date: "2027-05-31". Then we can parse results. If no events found, we can ask clarifying question. Let's do that.
